questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Romeo and Juliet was first performed at which type of London theatre?
questions.why: Shakespeare's plays, including Romeo and Juliet, were performed at open-air playhouses like the Globe, with daylight performances and no electric lighting.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: "Parting is such sweet sorrow" uses which technique?
questions.why: An oxymoron combines two contradictory ideas, like 'sweet sorrow', to capture mixed emotion in one phrase.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Bees carrying pollen between flowers is an example of which process?
questions.why: Cross-pollination happens when pollen moves from one plant to another, often carried by insects like bees, increasing genetic variation.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What year is generally given for Rome's fall?
questions.why: 476 CE is the traditionally cited year the last Western Roman emperor was deposed, marking the empire's fall.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: In the feudal pyramid, who stood directly below the king?
questions.why: Nobles received land directly from the king in exchange for loyalty and military support, placing them just below him in rank.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which quote shows love vs hate through contradiction?
questions.answer: "My only love sprung from my only hate"
questions.why: This line directly fuses love and hate in one contradictory statement, showing the theme through paradox, not romance alone.
options: "My only love sprung from my only hate"
"It is the east, and Juliet is the sun"

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which shows the medieval Church acting as a political power?
questions.why: Excommunication threatened a ruler's legitimacy and afterlife, giving the Church real political leverage over kings, unlike purely religious rituals.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A student argues that because Jerusalem was eventually lost by the Crusaders, the Crusades left no lasting mark on history. Which response best challenges this using a specific long-term effect?
questions.answer: Trade routes opened by the Crusades increased contact between Europe and the Middle East, spreading goods and ideas long after Jerusalem was lost
questions.why: Even after Jerusalem changed hands again, the Crusades opened lasting trade and cultural exchange between Europe and the Middle East — a significant effect that has nothing to do with who held the city.
options: Trade routes opened by the Crusades increased contact between Europe and the Middle East, spreading goods and ideas long after Jerusalem was lost
The Crusades were fought entirely for religious reasons, so military outcomes in Jerusalem were never really the point of the wars
European knights who survived the Crusades returned home with more land and titles than before they left for the Holy Land
The Crusades ended quickly after the first campaign, so their effects on trade and culture were too brief to matter much

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which of these best reflects a genuine fact about Shakespeare's life and the Globe Theatre?
questions.answer: Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon and later performed with his company at the Globe
questions.why: Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon and worked as an actor and playwright with the Lord Chamberlain's Men, who performed at the Globe. He didn't build the theatre himself, and Verona is the fictional setting of Romeo and Juliet, not his hometown.
options: Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon and later performed with his company at the Globe
Shakespeare was born in London and built the Globe Theatre himself with his own money
Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon but never performed in London theatres at all
Shakespeare was born in Verona and moved to London to write for the Globe company

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which best explains why the balcony scene shows more than 'just romance'?
questions.answer: Shakespeare uses light and dark imagery, comparing Juliet to the sun, to elevate her importance and foreshadow the intensity of their doomed love
questions.why: The balcony scene uses light/dark imagery and metaphor, not just romantic dialogue — this technique elevates Juliet and hints at the emotional stakes ahead.
options: Shakespeare uses light and dark imagery, comparing Juliet to the sun, to elevate her importance and foreshadow the intensity of their doomed love
The scene is written in simple prose so the audience can easily follow a straightforward romantic conversation between the two lovers
The scene relies mainly on stage directions describing physical movement rather than any language technique or imagery
The scene uses comic relief through the Nurse's jokes to lighten the romantic mood between Romeo and Juliet

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A gardener notices a spider plant growing small identical plantlets on runners with no flowers involved. Which term best describes this reproduction, and why?
questions.answer: Asexual reproduction, because only one parent is involved and the offspring are genetically identical to it
questions.why: Asexual reproduction needs only one parent and produces genetically identical offspring, exactly as seen with spider plant runners forming clones without flowers or gametes.
options: Asexual reproduction, because only one parent is involved and the offspring are genetically identical to it
Sexual reproduction, because two separate plant structures combined their genetic material to form the plantlets
Cross-pollination, because the plantlets formed after pollen was transferred between two separate flowers
Fertilisation, because male and female gametes joined together inside the runner to create new plantlets

questions.prompt: A classmate says the Crusades are barely worth studying because they were 'religious wars fought over a city that changed hands again anyway.' Using your own reasoning, explain what this view overlooks — pick one specific long-term effect (such as trade, cultural exchange, or the growth of Italian port cities) and explain how it shows the Crusades mattered beyond who controlled Jerusalem.
